title: an aliased context key charges exactly ["Clock"], so the matching layer subtracts it and the program runs
notes: THE ACCEPTANCE HALF of the round-7 context-key family, and the only case in it that can tell 'charges the Clock row' from 'charges A row'. specification/requirements.mdx:34 (Locked): `Capability.context()` 'MUST return the receiving capability's instance type and add that class's nominal identity to the enclosing function's inferred `R` row', and :78: a Layer providing that capability discharges it. Its three refusing siblings — 05-context-rows/a-const-alias-context-key-charges-the-same-row and the parenthesised and satisfies-wrapped spellings — each declare one SMITHERS2102 with the capability's name, which pins that SOMETHING unsatisfied named `Clock` was reported; none of them can observe that the row is EXACTLY `["Clock"]`, because an over-charged row is unsatisfied too and satisfies the same expectation. Here the layer supplies `Clock` and nothing else, so the program compiles only if the row is exactly what the layer provides, and it PRINTS only if the recognizer also LOWERED the access to the real context read. That second half is not rhetorical: the round-7 defect was measured as a program that compiled clean with `requirements: []` and then died at run time with `capability 'Clock' was not provided`, so a case that stopped at 'compiles' would have been green over it. This is the same shape as 05-context-rows/a-capability-read-through-a-local-alias-is-subtracted-by-its-layer, which is the alias-of-the-RECEIVER guard; this is the alias-of-the-KEY guard, and the two rules are different helpers. The over-refusal direction of the same helper is guarded from the host-global side by 20-host-globals/an-aliased-pure-member-key-needs-no-capability.
